content.Recommendations for imaging for patients: In patients with no recurrence of chest pain, normal ECG findings, and normal levels of cardiac troponin but still with suspected ACS, a non-invasive test (preferably with imaging) for inducible ischaemia or CCTA is recommended before deciding on an invasive approach. In patients with suspected ACS, non-elevated (or uncertain) hs-cTn, no ECG changes and no recurrence of pain, incorporating CCTA or a non-invasive stress imaging test as part of the initial workup should be considered.
content.Recommendations for timing of invasive s: An early invasive strategy within 24 h is recommended in patients with any of the following high-risk criteria: diagnosis of NSTEMI suggested by diagnostic algorithm; dynamic or presumable new contiguous ST/T-segment changes suggesting ongoing ischaemia; transient ST-segment elevation; GRACE risk score >140. An early invasive strategy within 24 h should be considered in patients with at least one of the listed high-risk criteria.
content.Recommendations for antiplatelet and ant: A potent P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel or ticagrelor), or clopidogrel if these are not available or are contraindicated, is recommended before (or at latest at the time of) PCI and maintained over 12 months unless contraindicated. Pre-treatment with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor may be considered in patients undergoing a primary PCI strategy.
content.Recommendations for long-term antithromb: After stent implantation in patients undergoing a strategy of DAPT, stopping aspirin after 3–6 months should be considered depending on balance of ischaemic and bleeding risks. In patients who are event-free after 3–6 months of DAPT and who are not high ischaemic risk, SAPT (preferably with a P2Y12 receptor inhibitor) should be considered.
content.Recommendations for cardiac arrest and o: Delayed as opposed to immediate angiography should be considered among haemodynamically stable patients without ST-segment elevation successfully resuscitated after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Targeted temperature management aiming for a constant temperature between 32 and 36°C for at least 24 h is recommended in patients who remain unconscious after resuscitation.
content.Recommendations for in-hospital manageme: When echocardiography is suboptimal/inconclusive, an alternative imaging method (CMR preferably) should be considered.
content.Recommendations for management of multiv: Complete revascularisation is recommended either during the index PCI procedure or within 45 days.
content.Recommendations for acute coronary syndr: Glucose-lowering therapy should be considered in ACS patients with blood glucose >10 mmol/L (>180 mg/dL), targeting avoidance of hypoglycaemia. Glucose-lowering therapy should be considered in patients with ACS with persistent hyperglycaemia, while episodes of hypoglycaemia should be avoided.

Associated Conditions: Long-term antiplatelet (single antiplatelet) therapy after DAPT
